html:
The Kitanemuk are an Indigenous people of southern California who lived in the Tehachapi Mountains and the Antelope Valley, on the western edge of the Mojave Desert in today's Kern County. They spoke a Takic language related to that of the Serrano.

They gathered acorns, pinyon nuts and seeds, hunted, and traded between the coast and the desert. Their neighbours were the Yokuts to the north, the Kawaiisu to the east, the Chumash to the west and the Tataviam and Tongva to the south. Many were taken into the missions at San Fernando and San Gabriel. Later the Tejon Ranch and a short lived reservation held their descendants, who are now part of the Tejon Indian Tribe.
